answer:
Usually, no. Most studies find intermittent fasting and daily calorie restriction produce similar weight loss when they create a similar calorie deficit. A 2025 trial found one exception: a 4:3 plan (three days of substantial restriction each week) led to greater average weight loss after a year—7.6% versus 5%—but that result was specific to that plan and doesn’t mean all forms of fasting work better. [1][2]

The practical choice is the approach you can sustain. Intermittent fasting may help some people eat less by limiting when they eat; daily calorie restriction may suit others better. Either way, the calorie deficit over time is the main driver of weight loss. [1]
